title: Myth vs Fact: Pouring Boiling Water Down PVC Drains
description: Many homeowners and DIYers believe pouring boiling water down a clogged PVC drain will melt grease and safely clear the system. In reality, boiling water reaches 212°F (100°C), which exceeds the continuous operating temperature rating of standard PVC schedule 40 drainage piping (typically rated around 140°F). Excessive heat can soften pipe walls, warp thin-walled traps, or degrade rubber seals and glued joints. Furthermore, melted grease merely travels further into the cold underground drainage network, cooling down and re-solidifying deeper in the main sewer line. Professional plumbers rely on mechanical snaking or targeted hydro-jetting to remove grease build-up safely without damaging the piping structure.

Excessive heat can soften pipe walls, warp thin-walled traps, or degrade rubber seals and glued joints. Furthermore, melted grease merely travels further into the cold underground drainage network, cooling down and re-solidifying deeper in the main sewer line. Professional plumbers rely on mechanical snaking or targeted hydro-jetting to remove grease build-up safely without damaging the piping structure.
